title: Vertex Cloud x Redwood - Partner intro
next_steps: Send partner one-pager and integration checklist
Schedule technical deep dive with Vertex infra team (Maya + Marco)
Share benchmark spreadsheet and example pricing scenarios for Dedicated vs Hosted
action_items: Sanjay: Send Vertex partner one-pager and Redwood partner deck by 2025-11-22
Maya: Setup a tech deep dive meeting and invite Marco and Vertex infra (propose 11/27 or 11/28)
Marco: Share current GPU instance mix and estimated monthly usage by 2025-11-24
Liam: Intro to Vertex legal contact for NDA and reseller terms by 2025-11-25
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood (AE+SE) and Vertex Cloud to explore cloud/GPU reseller and integration opportunities. Covered Vertex's go-to-market for GPU infra, potential reseller margins, integration touchpoints (billing, onboarding, API routing), and next steps for a technical deep dive and legal intro.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted model for partners
transcript:
[00:00] Sanjay Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate you making time today. I'm Sanjay, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. With me is Maya Chen, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Hi Sanjay, thanks. Liam here, Head of Partnerships at Vertex Cloud. Also with me Priya and Marco.
[00:18] Dr. Priya Rao: Hi all. Excited to learn more — we've been watching Redwood's latency stuff, interesting.
[00:24] Maya Chen: Awesome thanks. Quick agenda, we'll do intros, high level on Redwood, then dig into Vertex infra and where we might partner, and finish with next steps. Sound okay?
[00:33] Marco Diaz: Yeah sounds good. We'll keep it tight, we have folks in APAC but good to kick things off.
[00:41] Sanjay Patel: Cool — super quick intros: I've been running partner motion for Redwood for two years now, focus on cloud resellers and SI. Maya is our lead SE for infra partnerships — she owns benchmarks and POCs.
[00:50] Maya Chen: Hi all. I usually do the heavy lifting on latency tests and Dedicated infra sizing.
[00:58] Liam O'Connor: Priya runs product, Marco is our lead on integrations and infra.
[01:05] Dr. Priya Rao: On the Vertex side, we've got a mix of custom GPU nodes — mostly A100 and H100 fleet, plus a growing Ampere 4 fleet, and we partner with a couple of colo providers. We focus on predictable SLAs for enterprise customers.
[01:24] Sanjay Patel: Nice. Quick question — is Vertex primarily a reseller marketplace or do you sell managed infra?
[01:29] Marco Diaz: We do both. We provide managed clusters for customers who want our ops, and we also surface partner images in our marketplace. Typical enterprise buys the managed offering.
[01:38] Maya Chen: Great. From Redwood's perspective, there are a few partnership flavors we see — reseller, joint go-to-market, or infrastructure integration where Vertex could be a Dedicated capacity host for Redwood Dedicated.
[01:51] Liam O'Connor: We're most interested in reseller + hosting Dedicated. Our sales team likes the recurring revenue split. Curious how Redwood handles pricing and routing across hosted and dedicated.
[02:02] Sanjay Patel: Short answer: we have a hosted API and a Dedicated model. Hosted is straightforward revenue share; Dedicated is reserved capacity — you host pools and we route tenant workloads there if they choose. There's also private deployment for very sensitive customers.
[02:18] Marco Diaz: When you say routing, do you mean at request time? How flexible are the routing policies?
[02:24] Maya Chen: Yeah, we have policy-driven smart routing — latency, cost, region. You can build rules like prefer Dedicated for enterprise accounts, fallback to hosted if capacity is low, or route based on model capability.
[02:38] Marco Diaz: Ok. What about billing integration? Our marketplace needs to show per-customer billing and get invoicing details.
[02:45] Sanjay Patel: We usually integrate via a partner billing connector or use a reseller agreement where Vertex invoices customers and then we invoice Vertex. We can support metered usage exports and per-tenant cost reports — Maya, you want to add?
[02:58] Maya Chen: Yes, we expose token-level usage and per-route metrics. For Dedicated, we can push usage records or provide access to billing endpoints. Some partners prefer receiving aggregated monthly invoices, others handle raw events. We also have quota and rate-limiting hooks.
[03:14] Dr. Priya Rao: Security is obviously big for our enterprise customers. Do you have SOC 2, ISO, SSO integrations?
[03:21] Sanjay Patel: We are SOC 2 Type II and have Enterprise SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC, and KMS integrations for Private deployments. For Dedicated, audit logs and tenant-level isolation are standard.
[03:34] Liam O'Connor: Good. A lot of our customers ask about on-prem and VPC peering — can Redwood run in customer VPCs?
[03:41] Maya Chen: Yes, we offer Redwood Private that can be deployed in customer VPCs or on-prem. The on-prem package is more work but doable; it includes KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging. Our SEs will need to scope network and storage.
[03:55] Marco Diaz: From an infra angle, we'd need to know kernel-level optimizations — memory bandwidth, NVLink topology — to size Dedicated pools correctly. Do you publish perf profiles per model?
[04:07] Maya Chen: We publish model performance guides and have internal perf profiles for common models and sequence lengths. For Deep technical customers we run benchmarks on sample workloads to determine tokens/sec and GPU utilization. We can share a spreadsheet.
[04:20] Sanjay Patel: If it's helpful, we can run a quick benchmark with one of your H100 instances — measure latency and throughput on e.g., Llama2-70B quantized and a 1-shot chat workload.
[04:31] Marco Diaz: That'd be useful. Pricing will depend heavily on memory footprint and batch sizes. How does Redwood handle quantized models — do you support Q8/Q4 and is that exposed to partners?
[04:41] Maya Chen: We support quantization profiles; our runtime selects kernels and quantization paths. Partners can choose suggested profiles in Dedicated configs; for hosted we automatically pick optimized paths. Sometimes transcription has errors — we call our Dedicated product 'Redwood Dedicat' in notes — sorry.
[04:58] Dr. Priya Rao: Ha, noted. On GTM, we have a channel program that includes co-marketing credits and joint webinars. What has worked historically for Redwood partnerships?
[05:07] Sanjay Patel: Co-marketing with benchmark-led case studies works well, especially when we can show latency/cost delta vs competitors. We often do joint PR and a reference POC with one anchor customer.
[05:18] Liam O'Connor: Speaking of competitors, customers often compare to AWS Bedrock and CoreWeave for dedicated infra.
[05:25] Maya Chen: We see that. Our differentiator is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and the cost controls like KV/prefix caching and batching. Also our routing fallbacks are good for reliability.
[05:37] Marco Diaz: On the technical side, can we get a sense of networking requirements for Dedicated? Expected egress, p99 latencies, and any firewall rules?
[05:47] Maya Chen: We'll send a deployment checklist that includes peering, NAT configs, and port lists. For p99 targets, we generally target sub-100ms for chat on optimized pathways but it depends on model and token length.
[06:00] Sanjay Patel: Quick note — if Vertex wants to host Dedicated pools for multiple customers, we can support multi-tenant isolation at the buffer level; we'd need to discuss tenant quotas and eviction policies.
[06:12] Marco Diaz: Good. One more commercial question — revenue split expectation for reseller deals?
[06:17] Sanjay Patel: It's negotiable based on volume and support commitments; partners who commit to reserved capacity get better margins. We can do a template partner agreement and a sample margin sheet.
[06:28] Liam O'Connor: Ok good. We'll need that template and also a legal contact to discuss reseller terms.
[06:34] Sanjay Patel: We'll send defaults and loop in legal — action item.
[06:38] Dr. Priya Rao: What about support SLAs and runbook access? Enterprises need playbooks.
[06:44] Maya Chen: For Dedicated and Private we provide runbooks, playbooks, and a support tier. There's an on-call escalation path and we can integrate with Partner's ops channels.
[06:53] Marco Diaz: For the benchmark you proposed, what's the minimal artifact you need from us?
[06:58] Maya Chen: GPU instance details (model, vram, interconnect), expected concurrency, and a representative prompt set. If you can share a small prompt set and a docker image or AMI we can run tests in your environment.
[07:12] Marco Diaz: We'll compile that and share.
[07:16] Liam O'Connor: Timeline-wise, we're aiming to have a pilot with one joint customer in Q1 2026. Is that feasible?
[07:23] Sanjay Patel: Yes that's realistic. Pilot -> POC -> production cadence works; target for pilot kickoff in Jan.
[07:29] Dr. Priya Rao: Great. For compliance, some customers require data residency in EU. Does Redwood have regional hosting options?
[07:36] Maya Chen: Yes, we have hosted regions in EU and can run Dedicated in those regions. Private deployments support customer-managed networking in-region as well.
[07:45] Sanjay Patel: All right, I think we covered the main topics. We'll share partner deck, bench spreadsheet, and legal template. Any other questions?
[07:53] Marco Diaz: Not from me. I'll follow up with infra details.
[07:57] Liam O'Connor: We'll look for the deck and schedule the tech deep dive.
[08:02] Sanjay Patel: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and next steps.
[08:06] [meeting ends]
